label: Possible sepsis
message: A fever together with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin or a collapsing blood pressure can mean infection is affecting the whole body.
action: Call emergency services now. Do not wait to see whether it settles.

label: Rash that does not fade under pressure
message: Spots that stay visible when a glass is pressed on them, alongside feeling unwell, can be a sign of bacteria in the bloodstream.
action: Call emergency services now.

label: Possible severe allergic reaction
message: Swelling of the throat or tongue with difficulty breathing after a food, sting, or medicine can close the airway within minutes.
action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

label: Widespread rash with breathing difficulty
message: Hives together with breathing trouble, facial swelling or faintness is a whole-body allergic reaction.
action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

label: Reduced consciousness
message: Being difficult to rouse, or drifting in and out of awareness, always needs immediate assessment whatever the cause.
action: Call emergency services now. Place the person on their side if unresponsive.

label: Chest pain pattern suggesting the heart
message: Central chest pressure that spreads to the arm or jaw, or comes with a cold sweat, is treated as a heart attack until proven otherwise.
action: Call emergency services now. Chew 300 mg aspirin unless you are allergic or have been told not to.

label: Tearing chest pain
message: A tearing or ripping pain going through to the back, at full force from the first moment, can mean a tear in the main artery from the heart.
action: Call emergency services now. Do not take aspirin.

label: Possible clot on the lung
message: Breathlessness that began suddenly, with pain on breathing in or a swollen calf, can mean a clot has travelled to the lungs.
action: Go to an emergency department now, or call emergency services.

label: Sudden one-sided chest pain with breathlessness
message: Sudden sharp one-sided chest pain with breathlessness can mean a lung has partly collapsed.
action: Go to an emergency department now.

label: Severe breathing difficulty
message: An oxygen level below 94 percent, or being unable to speak a full sentence, means the lungs are not keeping up.
action: Call emergency services now.

label: Blackout with exertion or palpitations
message: Passing out during exercise, or alongside a racing heart or chest pain, can point to a dangerous heart rhythm rather than a simple faint.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment and an ECG. Do not drive.

label: Possible stroke
message: Sudden facial drooping, arm weakness or difficulty speaking is a stroke until proven otherwise. Treatment works only within a few hours.
action: Call emergency services now and note the exact time symptoms began.

label: Thunderclap headache
message: A headache that reaches its absolute worst within a minute can mean bleeding around the brain, even if it later eases.
action: Go to an emergency department now for a brain scan.

label: Headache with neck stiffness and fever
message: A stiff neck that will not let your chin reach your chest, with fever or a dislike of light, can mean infection around the brain.
action: Call emergency services now.

label: New headache with scalp tenderness in an older adult
message: A new headache after 50 with a tender scalp, an aching jaw on chewing, or visual change can inflame the arteries supplying the eye and cause blindness.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Blood tests and steroid treatment should not wait until tomorrow.

label: New headache with scalp tenderness in midlife
message: A new headache with a tender scalp or jaw ache on chewing needs inflammatory blood tests urgently.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment.

label: Headache pattern suggesting raised pressure in the head
message: A steadily worsening headache that is worst on waking, or made worse by coughing and straining, with vomiting, needs a brain scan.
action: Seek urgent medical assessment today for imaging.

label: Seizure
message: A first seizure needs assessment to find the cause and to advise on driving and safety.
action: Seek urgent assessment today. Call emergency services if the seizure lasted over five minutes or a second one followed.

label: Rigid, exquisitely tender abdomen
message: An abdomen that is hard and too tender to touch or move suggests inflammation spreading across the abdominal lining.
action: Go to an emergency department now. Do not eat or drink.

label: Possible bowel obstruction
message: Vomiting with a swelling abdomen and no wind passing at all suggests the bowel is blocked.
action: Go to an emergency department now. Do not eat or drink.

label: Significant gastrointestinal bleeding
message: Vomiting blood, or passing black tarry stools, means bleeding inside the digestive tract.
action: Go to an emergency department now.

label: Pain pattern suggesting appendicitis
message: Pain settling low on the right, especially if it began near the navel and came with loss of appetite, needs surgical assessment.
action: Seek same-day surgical assessment. Do not eat or drink.

label: Pelvic pain with a missed period
message: One-sided pelvic pain with a late or missed period can mean a pregnancy growing outside the womb, which can bleed suddenly and heavily.
action: Take a pregnancy test and go to an emergency department or early pregnancy unit today.

label: Sudden severe testicular pain
message: A testicle that becomes suddenly and severely painful may have twisted and lost its blood supply. It can only be saved within a few hours.
action: Go to an emergency department now. Do not eat or drink.

label: New jaundice
message: Yellowing of the skin or eyes always needs blood tests to find out why.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment.

label: Possible diabetic emergency
message: Heavy thirst and passing large volumes of urine, with vomiting or deep rapid breathing, can mean the blood has turned acidic.
action: Check blood glucose and ketones if you can, and call emergency services.

label: Possible cauda equina syndrome
message: Back pain with numbness around the groin, or new loss of bladder or bowel control, means nerves at the base of the spine are being crushed. Damage becomes permanent within hours.
action: Go to an emergency department now. This cannot wait until morning.

label: Back pain with cancer red flags
message: New back pain in someone with a history of cancer needs imaging to rule out spread to the spine.
action: Seek urgent medical assessment within 24 hours.

label: Back pain with fever
message: Back pain with fever, night pain or a weakened immune system can mean infection in the spine.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment and blood tests.

label: Possible deep vein thrombosis
message: One swollen, tender, warm calf can be a clot in a deep vein, which may travel to the lungs.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment for a scan and blood test. Go to an emergency department if you also become breathless or develop chest pain.

label: Cold, pale, pulseless limb
message: A limb that is cold, white, numb and has no pulse has lost its blood supply. Muscle dies within hours.
action: Call emergency services now. Keep the limb level, do not raise or warm it.

label: Hot swollen joint with fever
message: A single hot, swollen joint that cannot be moved, with fever, may be infected. Cartilage is destroyed within days.
action: Go to an emergency department today for the joint to be aspirated.

label: Spreading skin infection with fever
message: A hot red area of skin that is spreading, with fever, needs antibiotics started promptly.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Mark the edge of the redness with a pen so spread can be judged.

label: Painful red eye with visual change
message: A painful red eye with halos around lights, an odd-looking pupil or reduced vision can mean pressure inside the eye has risen dangerously.
action: Go to an eye emergency department now. Sight can be lost within hours.

label: Sudden loss of vision
message: Sight lost suddenly in one or both eyes needs assessment the same hour, whatever the cause.
action: Go to an eye emergency department now.

label: Swelling around the eye with fever
message: Swelling around the eye with fever and pain on moving the eye can mean infection behind the eye, which can spread to the brain.
action: Go to an emergency department now.

label: Sore throat with airway warning signs
message: A sore throat with drooling, a muffled voice, or difficulty breathing may mean the airway is narrowing.
action: Call emergency services now. Stay sitting upright and stay calm. Do not put anything in the mouth.

label: Ear pain with swelling behind the ear
message: Redness and swelling of the bone behind the ear, pushing the ear forward, means infection has spread beyond the middle ear.
action: Go to an emergency department today.

label: Coughing up blood
message: Coughing up blood always needs a chest X-ray, particularly in a smoker or former smoker.
action: Seek medical assessment within 24 hours for a chest X-ray.

label: Persistent cough with weight loss
message: A cough lasting over three weeks with weight loss or night sweats needs imaging to exclude serious lung disease.
action: Arrange a chest X-ray and medical review within two weeks.

label: Bowel changes needing urgent investigation
message: A lasting change in bowel habit with bleeding, weight loss or anaemia needs urgent investigation of the bowel.
action: Request an urgent referral and a stool blood test within two weeks.

label: Food sticking on swallowing
message: Food that sticks going down, especially with weight loss, needs an urgent camera test of the gullet.
action: Request an urgent endoscopy referral within two weeks.

label: Thoughts of self-harm
message: Thoughts of harming yourself or of being better off dead deserve help today. You do not have to be in crisis to reach out.
action: Contact your doctor, a crisis line, or go to an emergency department now. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

label: Losing fluid faster than it can be replaced
message: Enormous watery diarrhoea empties the body faster than drinking can keep up. Whatever the cause, the danger in the first hours is dehydration, not the infection.
action: Start oral rehydration salts now and keep drinking between every episode. Go to an emergency department if you cannot keep fluids down, stop passing urine, or feel faint on standing.

label: New confusion coming on over hours or days
message: Confusion that has come on over hours or days, or that comes and goes through the day, is delirium until proven otherwise. It is caused by something else -- an infection, a drug, pain, retention -- and that cause needs finding today.
action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Take a list of all medications. Call emergency services if they are drowsy, feverish or cannot be roused properly.

label: Limb-threatening injury
message: An open wound down to the bone, a limb that has gone cold or pale, or pain that keeps building far beyond what the injury explains, can mean the blood supply or the muscle compartment is compromised. Tissue can be lost within hours.
action: Go to an emergency department now. Do not eat or drink in case surgery is needed. Keep the limb still and at heart level.
